description: HW1-PIPE-v1 outer channel, inner protocol v2, X2: negative and boundary vectors with the P4 outcome, and P4-to-phone vectors with the answer the phone owes (a refusal, or CLOSE_ACK for a console CLOSE that crossed one). Same synthetic keys as phone_pipe_v2_sessions.json.
generated_by: components/hardwareone/test/host/phone_session_vectors.cpp: production BLE_PhoneGatt.cpp, BLE_PhoneSecureChannel.h, BLE_PhonePipeCore.h and BLE_PhonePipeConsoleCore.h on the synthetic SDK in phone_gatt_fake_sdk.h; only the device key, secure nonce and pipe HELLO nonce are fixed

base.handshake: Frames start at the P4 CCCD write of a fresh MTU-247 session (t_ms 0).
base.pipe_hello: Frames continue the MTU-247 session of phone_pipe_v2_sessions.json after the P4's pipe HELLO (frames 0-5: P4 counter 1 and inner sequence 0 are used); the phone's next frame is counter 1, inner sequence 0. A p4_to_phone vector at this stage takes the place of that HELLO (same counter 1, sequence 0).
base.pipe: Frames continue the MTU-247 session of phone_pipe_v2_sessions.json after the phone pipe HELLO_ACK (frames 0-6): phone outer counter 1 and inner sequence 0 are used, P4 counter 1 and inner sequence 0 are used. Unless a vector says otherwise, phone frames use the next counter/seq and P4 frames continue at counter 2, sequence 1.
base.transport: No authenticated state; the adapter stops before the CCCD write.

fields.source: p4_production = outcome decided by the production P4 adapter; contract = P4-produced bytes and the answer Android owes under the agreed rule named in "rule" (a refusal, or CLOSE_ACK for a console CLOSE that crossed one); contract_synthetic = P4-to-phone bytes no production P4 writes, sealed with the P4-to-phone key under the counter and sequence the P4 would use, which Android must refuse under "rule"
fields.p4_sends_hex: values the P4 wrote after the first vector frame (REJECT, replies)
fields.auth_cooldown: the P4 charges its global 30 s authentication cooldown
fields.p4_error: the adapter session end reason: for an authenticated frame the pipe refuses, the core's own cause (a phone RESET's code, Flow, Protocol); Unauthorized only for frames that fail authentication
fields.version_signal: the P4 took the phone's stream-0 RESET 2 in Hello state as the version signal
fields.strike: the session counts as a version-mismatch strike for the owner (the version signal, or silence after the HELLO: link loss within 1500 ms or the 3 s HELLO deadline); three in a row latch "phone app too old"
fields.synthetic_frames: contract_synthetic only: the "i" of each frame no production P4 writes; the other frames are production P4 frames that set the vector up
fields.class: link (stream 0), relay, console (OPEN address type 4) or unopened (an id never opened)
fields.frame_order: the P4's order: its writes and receipts on its clock. Frames that crossed are listed as the P4 met them: a phone frame after a P4 frame the phone had not yet received (console_open_while_unwanted), or a P4 frame queued before a phone frame arrived and written after it (console_close_2_after_reset_1)
fields.refused_or_reset_ids: the phone accepts a P4 CLOSE with reason 0..5 on any id it has refused (OPEN_ERR) or reset (stream RESET) and answers CLOSE_ACK: the production P4 closes a console that the phone refused or reset when the two cross (console_open_while_unwanted: CLOSE 4; console_close_2_after_reset_1: CLOSE 2). The class bounds (relay 0..1, console 0..5) apply only to ids the phone still tracks as live; it never applies the relay bound to an id whose class it no longer tracks. The P4 keeps the same rule for the phone's CLOSEs
